text:
incidentbot: PAGERDUTY: page fired for service=redwood-runtime-prod route=gen/text (alert: high_95p_latency) - PD#PDTk9
oncall-bot: @alex you are the current primary oncall (rotation: alex -> priya). Paging now.

alex: acked. looking into it. any customer reports?

jamie: no customer tickets yet, monitoring shows a brief spike in 95p latency across us-west-2, started ~T-30s

alex: checking infra metrics and router logs now. running quick query:
```
# prometheus style
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[1m])) by (le))
```

alex: seeing 95p jump from ~220ms -> 1.6s for ~45s, then back to ~240ms. CPU on router-abc-3 jumped to 92% at the same time.

incidentbot: PagerDuty: alert auto-escalation to secondary (PD#PDTk9) - 60s since first page

priya: i'm awake, on stand-by. any access to the instance metrics? can you run `ssh router-abc-3` or check k8s pod?

alex: grabbing pod logs: `kubectl -n infra logs router-abc-3 -c envoy --since=2m | tail -n 200`
alex: found repeated 504s to backend pool (backend-gen-1) and a bunch of "upstream reset" traces. copying snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:05Z] envoy upstream reset: ECONNRESET from 10.10.22.45:9000
[2026-03-15T03:12:06Z] 504 response for req 0x3a9f
```

sre-lead: looks like brief backend flapping. could be autoscaler thrashing or a transient GPU OOM on the backend pods.

jamie: alerts show backend pod restarts around the spike window: backend-gen-1-5fde restarted twice within 1m.

alex: triggered a quick healthcheck against the backend pool:
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://backend.internal/health/gen || echo FAIL
```

alex: healthcheck returned ok after second attempt. Not seeing current errors. metrics indicate pod restart count=2 in last 2m.

incidentbot: PagerDuty: alert auto-resolved (PD#PDTk9) - condition cleared

priya: thanks. since it auto-resolved, I'm going to stay on for 10m and watch. can we suppress the alert flooding if the condition bounces quickly?

alex: agree. I think the alerting window is too narrow for this busy route. current rule: 1m eval, severity=page. propose change to 3m eval with a 2-minute flapping suppression window.

jamie: +1 to adjust window. also, autoscaler for backend-gen has min_replicas=2 and target_cpu=60%. if pods are getting GPU OOMs we might need to raise min_replicas to 3 for this model variant.

sre-lead: create a follow-up ticket to tune alerting and autoscale policy. alex/priya, please paste any relevant logs into the ticket. I'll own the postmortem if we see customer impact.

alex: filing ticket now: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4521 - included logs, prometheus graphs, and suggested alert tuning.

priya: handing off monitoring to @priya (I'll take watch for next 30m). alex you can stand down. thanks for fast ack and triage :thumbsup:

alex: thanks, handing off. I'll follow up on the ticket tomorrow and sync with infra team about PDB/oom settings.

incidentbot: On-call handoff recorded: primary -> priya at 03:14 UTC. rotation note attached.

jamie: quick note for runbook: add a bullet under "transient 95p spikes" — check backend pod restart counts before escalating to page. small changes like this can cut noisy pages.

priya: noted. will update runbook and set a temporary alert hold for the next 1 hour while we monitor.

sre-lead: good work team. no customer impact observed. keep an eye on it and escalate if it reappears.

alex: logging off, marking as resolved on my side. good catch everyone.

incidentbot: Thread closed (auto-resolve).
